messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) the equilibrium temperature at which liquid water turns into solid ice is **about –2 °C**.  
This follows from the water phase diagram: as the pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, the melting/freezing line slopes downward, so the freezing point drops. At the triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.006 atm) the freezing point is 0.01 °C, and at 0.1 atm it is roughly –2 °C.  

> **Note:** The exact value can vary slightly depending on the purity of the water and the presence of dissolved gases or solutes. In practice, pure water at 10 kPa will freeze at approximately –2 °C.
